title: Small $q$-kernels in digraphs with minimum in-degree $δ$
summary: For a digraph $D$, a subset $Q\subseteq V(D)$ is called a $q$-kernel if $Q$ is an independent set and all vertices in $V(D)$ are reachable from $Q$ via a directed path of length at most $q$. Given integers $q\geq 2$ and $δ\geq 1$, Spiro arXiv:2404.07305 [math.CO] posed the question: what is the smallest constant $c_{δ,q}$ such that every digraph $D$ with minimum in-degree $δ$ has a $q$-kernel of size at most $c_{δ,q}|V(D)|$?
